newsitem.title: UK: Drought not affecting Europe sugar beet yet - Licht.
newsitem.headline: Drought not affecting Europe sugar beet yet - Licht.

text.p: Drought conditions in western Europe's sugar beet areas should not affect crop growth as yet but rains will be needed in May to ensure stable germination, F.O. Licht said on Wednesday.
In its daily report, the German statistician said dry weather was expected to continue in the region's beet belt, where drillings were mostly completed this week, for at least another week.
"Crops are in no immediate danger from the persistent lack of rain, but more moisture will need to return in May to ensure stable germination and early development," Licht said.
The region saw below average precipitation in the week ended April 15, it added, noting that moisture reserves in Europe's eastern belt were adequate due to periodic showers during the past month.
According to independent forecaster WSC, near drought to drought conditions dominate western areas, including the major corn areas of France.
"Soil moisture is very low. Rain is needed. Conditions are not quite as bad in the east where frequent precipitation has occurred," WSC said in a report on Wednesday.
It forecast a short-term outlook from Friday to Sunday of very cool and unsettled in the east with fair and seasonably cool weather in the west.
